quote: The duck broth is seasoned with a soy-sauce tare; Japanese soy sauce is almost always wheat-fermented, so the broth should be treated as containing wheat/gluten.
found: 鴨と水だけでひいた鴨の特製スープで、上品で優しい味わいです。鴨らしい滋味深いを旨味と醤油のまろやかな風味に、甘くコクのある鴨脂が全体をまとめています。 / menu: 鴨と貝の中華そば（醤油・塩）
note: Page confirms a soy-sauce-seasoned duck broth (醤油の風味) and a 醤油 menu option; the wheat inference is general, not stated on the page. Page also confirms the noodles are 全粒粉 wheat from 麺屋棣鄂 — worth adding to the gf note.

quote: Broth is made from duck and water and finished with duck fat; bowls include duck loin and shellfish (clam/scallop) variants, so there is no plant-based base in the kitchen.
found: 鴨と水だけでひいた鴨の特製スープ / 仕上げに鴨脂を使用 / チャーシューは鴨ロースを使用 / 鴨と貝の中華そば
note: Fully supported except the parenthetical: the article says only 貝 (shellfish), never clam or scallop specifically — drop the over-specific gloss.

quote: Noodles are wheat-based (whole-grain + refined wheat flour) and boiled in shared water; no gluten-free option exists.
found: 長野産の石臼挽き全粒粉を小麦に練りだ粉の２種類をミックスした、自家製麺の細麺 / 国内産小麦を用いた細麺を使用しているのが特長
note: Wheat + whole-grain house noodles confirmed and no GF option appears anywhere on the page; 'shared boiling water' is our inference, not stated — reword. Page also shows the 浓厚海老つけ麺 is served with パン (bread), a second wheat item worth naming.

quote: All broths are animal-based (sweet-shrimp heads, chicken, seafood); shared cookware means no vegan-safe preparation.
found: １ｋｇ以上の甘海老の頭を炒め、さらに玉ネギ、人参など野菜の旨味を足し / 鶏魚介、辛味噌、豚バラの各つけ麺のベースは全て濃厚鶏魚介スープ / 鰹節・鯖節・煮干しなどの魚介でとったスープ
note: Every listed base is animal (shrimp heads, chicken, katsuo/saba/niboshi); claim holds.

why: Shop announced 【麺心よし田営業休止のお知らせ】「諸事情により、しばらくの間営業をお休みいたします」 on 2026-03-29 (X @yaokin7 / IG @menshinyoshida); last service 2026-03-31; osumituki's March 2026 Kyoto ramen roundup lists it as 無期限休業 (indefinite suspension) and pointedly NOT among the month's five 閉店; an IG reel of 2026-07-14 still says ⚠️現在休業中; Tabelog now shows 「このお店は店舗情報の確認が取れていないため掲載保留中です」. 休業, not 閉店 — suspended, not shut.

quote: Wheat ramen/tsukemen/mazesoba noodles (including whole-grain wheat flour) are boiled in shared water; not safe for celiac or wheat-allergic diners.
found: ツルシコの細麺は全粒粉入りで風味が良くおいしいです。 / まぜそばは茹で時間がかかるとのことでらぁ麺が先に到着しました。 / もっちりとした平打ち麺
note: Whole-grain wheat noodles for both らぁ麺 and まぜそば confirmed, and both are boiled; but this shop's menu on the page is らぁ麺/まぜそば/炙り叉焼丼/おいめし — there is no tsukemen, so drop that word. Shared boiling water is inference, not stated.

quote: The shoyu tare flavoring the broth is wheat-based soy sauce; allergen note lists wheat in both noodles and soy sauce.
found: 鴨と大山丸鶏の出汁がよく出たスープにキリッとした醤油が利いています。
note: First half holds (the page does describe a sharp 醤油 tare). Second half does not: the cited page contains no allergen note at all — the strings アレル and 小麦 appear nowhere on it, and no allergen table was found for this shop elsewhere. Delete the invented 'allergen note lists wheat' clause; the wheat-in-shoyu point must stand as a general-practice inference, not as a citation.

quote: Broth is chicken-and-duck stock and toppings include chicken and pork chashu and egg; no plant-based preparation, so all items carry animal cross-contact.
found: 鴨と大山丸鶏の出汁がよく出たスープ / トッピングは鶏チャーシュー、豚チャーシュー、穂先メンマ、玉ねぎ、三つ葉 / トリュフオイル漬けの卵黄とレモンが付属します
note: Duck + Daisen whole-chicken dashi, chicken and pork chashu, and a marinated egg yolk on the mazesoba — all on the cited page.

quote: The shop's two core bowls are shoyu-based ramen (chuka soba and sebabura shoyu). Soy-sauce tare in Japanese ramen is conventionally brewed with wheat; no wheat-free tare is mentioned by any source.
found: メニューは基本は「あっさり」の中華そば、「こってり」の背脂醤油の2種類です。 / こってりは「ベースは同じで、カエシが違い、背脂」というラーメンです。
note: Two-bowl shoyu menu confirmed verbatim; no wheat-free tare is claimed anywhere on the page. Page is from 2017 — the menu is old evidence, worth a fresher source.

quote: The broth is made from pork bone, chicken, kombu and seafood and the kitchen is built around animal-based ramen, so vegan diners face unavoidable contact with meat and fish stock throughout.
found: ベースは「豚骨・鶏ガラ・昆布・魚介」で、昆布・魚介の割合が少し多めの和風出汁に近いものになっていました。
note: Exact four-ingredient base quoted on the page; also 背脂 (back fat) in the こってり bowl. Claim holds.

quote: The menu centers on shoyu (soy-sauce-based) and shio chicken ramen; standard ramen shoyu tare is wheat-based, and no gluten-free tare is indicated.
found: 味付け（タレ）は醤油で辛さ控えめの京都ラーメンらしい味わい。 / メニュー：濃厚鶏白湯・旨辛スタミナ鶏白湯・こく旨鶏白湯・濃厚魚介（醤油or塩）・辛まぜそば・ライス
note: Soy tare confirmed and no GF tare anywhere on the page, but the framing is off: the house bowl is 濃厚鶏白湯 (chicken paitan, 醤油 tare) and the 醤油/塩 choice belongs to the 濃厚魚介 seafood bowl, not to a 'shio chicken ramen'. Same page also documents wheat noodles (太麺の平打ち縮れ麺 from 麺屋棣鄂) — cite that for the gf field, which currently has no source.

quote: All broths are animal-based (long-simmered chicken paitan/clear chicken soup) and bowls are topped with pork and chicken chashu, so vegan diners cannot be accommodated.
found: 名古屋コーチンなどの地鶏を3種類使い8時間煮詰めて旨味を引き出したスープ / 青ねぎ・白ねぎ・豚と鶏のレアチャーシューが2枚ずつ・メンマ・一味 / 表面には香味油（鶏油=チーユ）と背脂が浮かんで
note: Chicken paitan, pork+chicken chashu, chicken oil and back fat all confirmed; the fourth bowl (濃厚魚介) is fish, so 'all broths animal-based' still holds. No vegan option on the menu list.

quote: Bowls are built on house-made whole-wheat noodles plus white or black soy sauce tare; no gluten-free preparation is offered and shared cooking water makes the kitchen unsuitable for celiac diners.
found: The homemade noodles, made of stone-ground whole wheat flour, are thin but firm, and go well with the soup.
note: Whole-wheat house noodles and both tare confirmed; shared boiling water is our inference, not stated. WARNING about this very source: its machine translation calls the bowls 'dashi soba (buckwheat noodles)' twice — a celiac reading the cited English page could conclude buckwheat/gluten-free. Our record text should say explicitly that the noodles are wheat despite the word 'soba' on the page.

quote: The defining seasoning is white (shiro) or black (kuro) soy sauce tare, which is normally wheat-fermented.
found: In addition to dashi soba made with special white soy sauce (shiro shoyu), dashi soba made with mild and rich special dark black soy sauce (kuro shoyu) is also a popular menu item. / Dashi-soba (white soy sauce) 1,400 yen … The unique sweetness of white soy sauce matches the 100% seafood broth.
note: Understated rather than wrong: 白醤油 is not merely 'normally wheat-fermented', it is majority wheat by grain weight (the inverse of tamari). The signature 出汁そば（白醤油） is therefore the single highest-wheat bowl on the menu, and the record should say so instead of hedging with 'normally'.

quote: All bowls are based on a seafood (dried-fish) dashi, so no broth is free of animal-derived ingredients.
found: its soup, which is made from 100% seafood broth without any animal fat such as pork or chicken. The broth is made by blending several kinds of carefully selected top-quality fish knots and extracting them slowly at a low temperature
note: 'Fish knots' is the auto-translation of 魚節 (dried fish flakes). Fish is animal, so a 100%-seafood broth is emphatically not vegan; claim holds.

quote: The broth uniquely contains no pork or chicken fat — a 100% seafood dashi — which may matter to diners avoiding mammalian/poultry products specifically.
found: its soup, which is made from 100% seafood broth without any animal fat such as pork or chicken
note: Verbatim on the page. Keep the framing narrow — pescatarian-relevant only, and it must not read as any kind of gluten or vegan reassurance given the whole-wheat noodles and 白醤油 tare.
